title: The year Kuwait's sky went black at noon 🔥
subject: fire
description:
Could a fire this size be put out faster today? 👇

In February 1991, retreating Iraqi forces blew up 737 Kuwaiti oil wells. Smoke turned day into darkness, oily black rain fell as far as Iran and Central Asia, and more than 10,000 workers needed until 6 November 1991, 35 years ago this week, to cap the last well.

Sources: US Department of Defense, GulfLINK, "Oil Well Fires", Tab C: Fighting the Oil Well Fires; Kuwait Times / KUNA, "35 years since Kuwait extinguished last burning oil well" (6 Nov 2026); Wikipedia: Kuwaiti oil fires

scenes.text: In 1991, the midday sky over Kuwait went black.
Retreating Iraqi troops had blown up 737 oil wells.
Kuwait lost up to 6 million barrels a day, and under the smoke, temperatures fell about 4°C.
scenes.nasa: Kuwait oil fire smoke from space

scenes.text: Oily black rain fell as far away as Iran.
More than 10,000 workers from 37 countries fought the fires. One Hungarian team blew out flames with jet engines bolted onto tanks.
The last well, in the Burgan field, was capped on 6 November 1991.
